arXiv:0907.3990v2 [math.AC] 18 Jan 2010

A Deformation of Commutative Polynomial Algebras in Even Numbers of Variables

Wenhua Zhao
Abstract.

We introduce and study a deformation of commutative polynomial algebras in even numbers of variables. We also discuss some connections and applications of this deformation to the generalized Laguerre orthogonal polynomials and the interchanges of right and left total symbols of differential operators of polynomial algebras. Furthermore, a more conceptual re-formulation for the image conjecture [Z3] is also given in terms of the deformed algebras. Consequently, the well-known Jacobian conjecture [Ke] is reduced to an open problem on this deformation of polynomial algebras.

Key words and phrases: 
The generalized Laguerre polynomials, total symbols of differential operators, the image conjecture, the Jacobian conjecture.
2000 Mathematics Subject Classification
33C45, 32W99, 14R15

1. Introduction

Let ξ=(ξ1,ξ2,…,ξn)\xi=(\xi_{1},\xi_{2},...,\xi_{n}) and z=(z1,z2,…,zn)z=(z_{1},z_{2},...,z_{n}) be 2​n2n commutative free variables. Throughout this paper, we denote by ℂ⁡[ξ,z]\mathbb{C}[\xi,z], ℂ⁡[z]\mathbb{C}[z] and ℂ⁡[ξ]\mathbb{C}[\xi] the vector spaces (without any algebra structures) over ℂ\mathbb{C} of polynomials in (ξ,z)({\xi,z}), in zz and in ξ\xi, respectively. The corresponding polynomial algebras will be denoted respectively by 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[\xi,z], 𝒜⁡[z]{\mathcal{A}}[z] and 𝒜⁡[ξ]{\mathcal{A}}[\xi].

For any 1≤i≤n1\leq i\leq n, we set ∂i:=∂zi\partial_{i}\!:=\partial_{z_{i}} and δi=∂ξi\delta_{i}=\partial_{\xi_{i}}. Denote by ∂=(∂1,∂2,…,∂n)\partial=(\partial_{1},\partial_{2},...,\partial_{n}) and δ=(δ1,δ2,…,δn)\delta=(\delta_{1},\delta_{2},...,\delta_{n}). We also occasionally use ∂z\partial_{z} and ∂ξ\partial_{\xi} to denote ∂\partial and δ\delta, respectively.

Set Ω:=∑i=1n(∂i⊗δi+δi⊗∂i)\Omega\!:=\sum_{i=1}^{n}(\partial_{i}\otimes\delta_{i}+\delta_{i}\otimes\partial_{i}). For any t∈ℂt\in\mathbb{C}, we define a new product ∗t\ast_{t} for the vector space ℂ⁡[ξ,z]\mathbb{C}[\xi,z] by setting, for any f,g∈ℂ⁡[ξ,z]f,g\in\mathbb{C}[\xi,z],

(1.1) f∗tg:=μ⁡(e−t​Ω​(f⊗g)),\displaystyle f\ast_{t}g\!:=\mu\left(e^{-t\,\Omega}(f\otimes g)\right),

where μ:ℂ⁡[ξ,z]⊗ℂ⁡[ξ,z]→ℂ⁡[ξ,z]\mu:\mathbb{C}[\xi,z]\otimes\mathbb{C}[\xi,z]\to\mathbb{C}[\xi,z] denotes the product map of the polynomial algebra 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}].

Denote by ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}) the new algebra (ℂ[ξ,z],∗t)(\mathbb{C}[\xi,z],\ast_{t}). For the case t=1t=1, we also introduce the following short notation:

(1.2) ∗:\displaystyle\ast\!: =∗t=1.\displaystyle=\ast_{t=1}.
(1.3) ℬ⁡[ξ,z]:\displaystyle{\mathcal{B}}[{\xi,z}]\!: =ℬt=1​[ξ,z].\displaystyle={\mathcal{B}}_{t=1}[{\xi,z}].

Note that, when t=0t=0, the algebra ℬt=0​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t=0}[{\xi,z}] coincides with the usual polynomial algebra 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}].

In this paper, we first show that ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}) gives a deformation of the polynomial algebra 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}]. Actually, it is a trivial deformation in the sense of deformation theory. To be more precise, set

(1.4) Λ:\displaystyle\Lambda\!: =∑i=1nδi∂i.\displaystyle=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\delta_{i}\partial_{i}.
(1.5) Φt:\displaystyle\Phi_{t}\!: =et​Λ=∑m≥0tm​Λmm!.\displaystyle=e^{t\Lambda}=\sum_{m\geq 0}\frac{t^{m}\Lambda^{m}}{m!}.
(1.6) Φ:\displaystyle\Phi\!: =Φt=1.\displaystyle=\Phi_{t=1}.

Note that, Φt\Phi_{t} for any t∈ℂt\in\mathbb{C} is a well-defined bijective linear map from ℂ⁡[ξ,z]\mathbb{C}[\xi,z] to ℂ⁡[ξ,z]\mathbb{C}[\xi,z], whose inverse map is given by Φ−t=e−t​Λ\Phi_{-t}=e^{-t\Lambda}. This is because the differential operator Λ\Lambda of ℂ⁡[ξ,z]\mathbb{C}[\xi,z] is locally nilpotent, i.e. for any f⁡(ξ,z)∈ℂ⁡[ξ,z]f(\xi,z)\in\mathbb{C}[\xi,z], Λm​f​(ξ,z)=0\Lambda^{m}f(\xi,z)=0 when m≫0m\gg 0.

With the notation fixed above, we will show that, for any t∈ℂt\in\mathbb{C}, Φt:ℬt​[ξ,z]→𝒜⁡[ξ,z]\Phi_{t}:{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}]\to{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}] actually is an isomorphism of ℂ\mathbb{C}-algebras (See Proposition 2.1 and Corollary 2.2).

Note that, from the point view of deformation theory, the deformation ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}) is not interesting at all. But, surprisingly, as we will show in this paper, the algebra ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] and the isomorphism Φt\Phi_{t} are actually closely related with the generalized Laguerre polynomials (See [Sz], [PS] and [AAR]) and the interchanges of right and left total symbols of differential operators of polynomial algebras.

Furthermore, as we will show in Section 4, the algebras ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}) and the isomorphism Φt\Phi_{t} via their connections with the image conjecture proposed in [Z3] are also related with the Jacobian conjecture which was first proposed by O. H. Keller [Ke] in 19391939 (See also [BCW] and [E]). Actually, the Jacobian conjecture can be viewed as a conjecture which, in some sense, just claims that the algebra ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t≠0)(t\neq 0) should not differ or change too much from the polynomial algebra 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]=ℬt=0​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}]={\mathcal{B}}_{t=0}[{\xi,z}]. Therefore, from this point of view, the triviality of the deformation ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}) (in the sense of deformation theory) can be viewed as a fact in favor of the Jacobian conjecture. For another interesting application of the isomorphism Φ\Phi to the Jacobian conjecture, see [Z5].

Considering the length of the paper, below we give a more detailed description for the contents and the arrangement of the paper.

In Subsection 2.1, we prove some simple properties of the deformation ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}) and the isomorphism Φt:ℬt​[ξ,z]→𝒜⁡[ξ,z]\Phi_{t}:{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}]\to{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}], which will be needed for the rest of this paper. In particular, in this subsection the triviality of the deformation ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}) in the sense of deformation theory is proved in Proposition 2.1. and Corollary 2.2.

In Subsection 2.2, we show that, for different t∈ℂt\in\mathbb{C}, the ℓ\ell-adic topologies induced by ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] on the common base vector space ℂ⁡[ξ,z]\mathbb{C}[\xi,z] are different. But they are all homeomorphic to the ℓ\ell-adic topology induced by the polynomial algebra 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}] under the isomorphism Φt:ℬt​[ξ,z]→𝒜⁡[ξ,z]\Phi_{t}:{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}]\to{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}] (viewed as an automorphism of ℂ⁡[ξ,z]\mathbb{C}[\xi,z]). See Proposition 2.9 and also Corollary 2.10 for the precise statements.

In Subsection 2.3, we study the induced isomorphism (Φt)∗(\Phi_{t})_{*} (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}) of Φt\Phi_{t} from the differential operator algebra, or the Weyl algebra 𝒟t​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{D}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] of ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] to the Weyl algebra 𝒟⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{D}}[{\xi,z}] of 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}]. The main results of this subsection are Propositions 2.11 and 2.13. Proposition 2.11 says that the derivations ∂zi\partial_{z_{i}} and ∂ξi\partial_{\xi_{i}} (1≤i≤n)(1\leq i\leq n) of 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}] are also derivations of ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] for all t∈ℂt\in\mathbb{C} and are fixed by the isomorphism (Φt)∗(\Phi_{t})_{*}. Proposition 2.13 gives explicitly the images under (Φt)∗(\Phi_{t})_{*} of the multiplication operators with respect to the product ∗t\ast_{t} of ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}].

In Section 3, by using some results derived in Section 2, we show in Theorem 3.1 that Φ=Φt=1\Phi=\Phi_{t=1} (resp. Φt=−1\Phi_{t=-1}) as an automorphism of ℂ⁡[ξ,z]\mathbb{C}[\xi,z] actually coincides with the linear map which changes left (resp. right) total symbols of differential operators of 𝒜⁡[z]{\mathcal{A}}[z] to their right (resp. left) total symbols. Consequently, the products ∗t=±1\ast_{t=\pm 1} appear naturally when one derives left or right total symbols of certain differential operators of 𝒜⁡[z]{\mathcal{A}}[z] (See Corollary 3.2). The results derived in this subsection also play some important roles in [Z5] in which among some other results a more straightforward proof for the equivalence of the Jacobian conjecture and the vanishing conjecture (See [Z1] and [Z2]) will be given.

In Subsection 4.1, we study the Taylor series expansion of polynomials in ℂ⁡[ξ,z]\mathbb{C}[{\xi,z}] with respect to the new product ∗t\ast_{t} and use it to give a more conceptual proof for the expansion of polynomials given in Eq. (4.6). This expansion was first proved in [Z3] and played a crucial role there in the proof of the implication of the Jacobian conjecture from the image conjecture (See Conjecture 4.3).

In Subsection 4.2, we first recall the notion of the so-called Mathieu subspaces of commutative algebras (See Definition 4.2), which was first introduced in [Z4], and also the image conjecture (See Conjecture 4.3) for the differential operators ξi−t∂i\xi_{i}-t\partial_{i} (1≤i≤n)(1\leq i\leq n) in terms of the notion of Mathieu subspaces. We then give a re-formulation of Conjecture 4.3 in terms of the algebra ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}) (See Conjecture 4.5) and show in Theorem 4.6 that these two conjectures are equivalent to each other. Since it has been shown in [Z3] that Conjecture 4.3 implies Jacobian conjecture, hence so does Conjecture 4.5.

Consequently, via its connections with Conjecture 4.5, the Jacobian conjecture is reduced to an open problem on the deformation ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}) of the polynomial algebra 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}]. The open problem asks if the ideal ξ​ℂ​[ξ,z]\xi\mathbb{C}[{\xi,z}] of 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}] generated by ξ\xi will remain to be a Mathieu subspace in the algebra ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] for any t≠0t\neq 0. Note that any ideal is automatically a Mathieu subspace, but not conversely. Therefore, the triviality (in the sense of deformation theory) of the deformation ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}) proved in Proposition 2.1 can be viewed as a fact in favor of the Jacobian conjecture.

Section 5 is mainly on a connection of the algebra ℬ⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}[{\xi,z}], especially, its product ∗\ast with the multi-variable generalized Laguerre polynomials, and also some of the applications of this connection to both ℬ⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}[{\xi,z}] and the generalized Laguerre polynomials.

In Subsection 5.1, we very briefly recall the definition of the (generalized) Laguerre polynomials Lα[𝐤]​(z)L_{\alpha}^{[\bf k]}(z) (𝐤,α∈ℕn)({\bf k},\alpha\in{\mathbb{N}}^{n}) (See Eqs. (5.1)–(5.3)) and also the orthogonal property (See Theorem 5.1) of these polynomials.

In Subsection 5.2, we show in Theorem 5.2 that, for any 𝐤,α∈ℕn{\bf k},\alpha\in{\mathbb{N}}^{n}, we have

(1.7) Lα[𝐤]​(ξ​z)=(−1)|α|α!​ξ−𝐤​(ξα+𝐤∗zα)=(−1)|α|α!​z−𝐤​(ξα∗zα+𝐤).\displaystyle L_{\alpha}^{[{\bf k}]}(\xi z)=\frac{(-1)^{|\alpha|}}{\alpha!}\,\xi^{-\bf k}(\xi^{\alpha+{\bf k}}\ast z^{\alpha})=\frac{(-1)^{|\alpha|}}{\alpha!}\,z^{-{\bf k}}(\xi^{\alpha}\ast z^{\alpha+{\bf k}}).

Consequently, the generalized Laguerre polynomials Lα[𝐤]​(z)L_{\alpha}^{[\bf k]}(z) (𝐤,α∈ℕn)({\bf k},\alpha\in{\mathbb{N}}^{n}) can be obtained by evaluating the polynomials ξ−𝐤​(ξα+𝐤∗zα)\xi^{-\bf k}(\xi^{\alpha+{\bf k}}\ast z^{\alpha}) or z−𝐤​(ξα∗zα+𝐤)z^{-{\bf k}}(\xi^{\alpha}\ast z^{\alpha+{\bf k}}) at ξ=(1,1,…,1)\xi=(1,1,...,1). Note that the evaluation map at ξ=(1,1,…,1)\xi=(1,1,...,1) is not an algebra homomorphism from ℬ⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}[{\xi,z}] to 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}]. Otherwise, the generalized Laguerre polynomials would be trivialized.

In the first part of Subsection 5.3, we use certain results of the generalized Laguerre polynomials and the connection in Eq. (1.7) above to derive more properties on the polynomials ξα∗zα\xi^{\alpha}\ast z^{\alpha} which, by Proposition 2.6, (c)(c), are actually the monomials of ξ\xi and zz in the new algebra ℬ⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}[{\xi,z}].

For example, by using the connection in Eq. (1.7) and I. Schur’s irreducibility theorem [Sc1] of the Laguerre polynomials in one variable, we immediately have that, when n=1n=1, the monomials ξm∗zm\xi^{m}\ast z^{m} (m≥2)(m\geq 2) of ℬ⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}[{\xi,z}] are actually irreducible over ℚ{\mathbb{Q}} (See Theorem 5.9). Furthermore, by using I. Schur’s irreducibility theorem [Sc2] and M. Filaseta and T.-Y. Lam’s irreducibility theorem [FL] on the generalized Laguerre polynomials, we have that, all but finitely many of the polynomials ξ−k​(ξm+k∗zm)\xi^{-k}(\xi^{m+k}\ast z^{m}) and z−k​(ξm∗zm+k)z^{-k}(\xi^{m}\ast z^{m+k}) (m,k∈ℕ)(m,k\in{\mathbb{N}}) are irreducible over ℚ{\mathbb{Q}} (See Theorem 5.10).

In the second part of Subsection 5.3, we use the connection given in Eq. (1.7) and certain results of ℬ⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}[{\xi,z}] derived in Section 2 to give new proofs, first, for some recurrent formulas of the generalized Laguerre polynomials (See Proposition 5.11) and, second, for the fact that the generalized Laguerre polynomials satisfy the so-called associate Laguerre differential equation (See Theorem 5.12). At the end of this subsection, we draw the reader’s attention to a conjecture, Conjecture 5.13, on the generalized Laguerre polynomials, which is still open even for the classical Laguerre polynomials in one variable.

2. The Deformation ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] of the Polynomial Algebra 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}]

In this section, we first derive in Subsection 2.1 some properties and identities for the algebra ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}). In Subsection 2.2, we show that, for different t∈ℂt\in\mathbb{C}, the ℓ\ell-adic topologies induced by the algebras ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}) on the common base vector space ℂ⁡[ξ,z]\mathbb{C}[\xi,z] are different. But they are all homeomorphic under the isomorphism Φt:ℬt​[ξ,z]→𝒜⁡[ξ,z]\Phi_{t}:{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}]\to{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}] to the ℓ\ell-adic topology on ℂ⁡[ξ,z]\mathbb{C}[\xi,z] induced by the polynomial algebra 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}] (See Proposition 2.9 and also Corollary 2.10).

In Subsection 2.3, we study the isomorphism (Φt)∗(\Phi_{t})_{*} induced by Φt\Phi_{t} from the Weyl algebra of ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] to the Weyl algebra of 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}]. The main results in this subsection are Propositions 2.11 and 2.13.

2.1. Some Properties of the Algebras ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}]

In general, by Eqs. (2.4), (2.5) and also the induction assumption, we have

(2.6) ∂∂t​(f∗tg)=∂∂t​(f∗t′g).\displaystyle\frac{\partial}{\partial t}(f\ast_{t}g)=\frac{\partial}{\partial t}(f\ast_{t}^{\prime}g).

Since f∗tgf\ast_{t}g and f∗t′gf\ast_{t}^{\prime}g are polynomials in tt with coefficients in ℂ⁡[ξ,z]\mathbb{C}[{\xi,z}] and both satisfy Eqs. (2.3) and (2.6), it is easy to see that they must be equal to each other. Hence, Eq. (2.1) holds.  □\Box

Corollary 2.2.

For any t∈ℂt\in\mathbb{C}, Φt:ℬt​[ξ,z]→𝒜⁡[ξ,z]\Phi_{t}:{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}]\to{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}] is an isomorphism of algebras. Therefore, in the sense of deformation theory, the deformation ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] is a trivial deformation of the commutative polynomial algebra 𝒜⁡[ξ,z]{\mathcal{A}}[{\xi,z}].

Next we derive some properties of the algebras ℬt​[ξ,z]{\mathcal{B}}_{t}[{\xi,z}] (t∈ℂ)(t\in\mathbb{C}), which will be needed for the rest of this paper.

Lemma 2.3.

For any f,g∈ℂ⁡[ξ,z]f,g\in\mathbb{C}[{\xi,z}], we have

(2.7) f∗tg=∑α,β∈ℕn(−t)|α|+|β|α!​β!​(δβ​∂αf)​(∂βδα​g).\displaystyle f\ast_{t}g=\sum_{\alpha,\beta\in{\mathbb{N}}^{n}}\frac{(-t)^{|\alpha|+|\beta|}}{\alpha!\beta!}\,\,(\delta^{\beta}\partial^{\alpha}f)(\partial^{\beta}\delta^{\alpha}g).

Proof:  Note first that, for any 1≤i,j≤n1\leq i,j\leq n, ∂i⊗δi\partial_{i}\otimes\delta_{i} and δj⊗∂j\delta_{j}\otimes\partial_{j} commute with each other. So we have

(2.8) e−t​Ω\displaystyle e^{-t\,\Omega} =e−t∑i=1nδi⊗∂ie−t∑i=1n∂i⊗δi,\displaystyle=e^{-t\sum_{i=1}^{n}\delta_{i}\otimes\partial_{i}}\,e^{-t\sum_{i=1}^{n}\partial_{i}\otimes\delta_{i}},
(2.9) e−t∑i=1n∂i⊗δi\displaystyle e^{-t\sum_{i=1}^{n}\partial_{i}\otimes\delta_{i}} =∏i=1ne−t(∂i⊗δi)=∏i=1n∑ki≥0(−t)kiki!(∂iki⊗δiki)\displaystyle=\prod_{i=1}^{n}e^{-t(\partial_{i}\otimes\delta_{i})}=\prod_{i=1}^{n}\sum_{k_{i}\geq 0}\frac{(-t)^{k_{i}}}{k_{i}!}\,(\partial_{i}^{k_{i}}\otimes\delta_{i}^{k_{i}})
=∑α∈ℕn(−t)|α|α!(∂α⊗δα).\displaystyle=\sum_{\alpha\in{\mathbb{N}}^{n}}\frac{(-t)^{|\alpha|}}{\alpha!}\,\,(\partial^{\alpha}\otimes\delta^{\alpha}).

Similarly,

(2.10) e−t∑i=1nδi⊗∂i=∑β∈ℕn(−t)|β|β!(δβ⊗∂β).\displaystyle e^{-t\sum_{i=1}^{n}\delta_{i}\otimes\partial_{i}}=\sum_{\beta\in{\mathbb{N}}^{n}}\frac{(-t)^{|\beta|}}{\beta!}\,\,(\delta^{\beta}\otimes\partial^{\beta}).

Then it is easy to see that Eq. (2.7) follows directly from Eq. (1.1) and the last three equations above.  □\Box

Proposition 2.4.

(a)(a) For any λi​(ξ)∈ℂ​[ξ]\lambda_{i}(\xi)\in\mathbb{C}[\xi], pi​(z)∈ℂ​[z]p_{i}(z)\in\mathbb{C}[z] (i=1,2)(i=1,2), we have

(2.12) p1​(z)∗tp2​(z)\displaystyle p_{1}(z)\ast_{t}p_{2}(z) =p1​(z)​p2​(z).\displaystyle=p_{1}(z)p_{2}(z).

Proof:  Eqs. (2.11)–(2.13) follow directly from Eq. (2.7).

To show Eq. (2.14), first, by Eq. (2.7), we have

=∑α∈ℕn(−1)|α|​t|α|α!​(δα​λ​(ξ))​(∂αg⁡(ξ,z)).\displaystyle=\sum_{\alpha\in{\mathbb{N}}^{n}}\frac{(-1)^{|\alpha|}t^{|\alpha|}}{\alpha!}(\delta^{\alpha}\lambda(\xi))(\partial^{\alpha}g({\xi,z})).

Hence, Eq. (2.14) follows from the last two equations. Eq. (2.15) can be proved similarly.  □\Box

Lemma 2.5.

For any t∈ℂt\in\mathbb{C}, λ⁡(ξ)∈ℂ⁡[ξ]\lambda(\xi)\in\mathbb{C}[\xi] and p⁡(z)∈ℂ⁡[z]p(z)\in\mathbb{C}[z], we have

(2.18) Φt​(λ​(ξ))\displaystyle\Phi_{t}(\lambda(\xi)) =λ⁡(ξ).\displaystyle=\lambda(\xi).
(2.19) Φt​(p​(z))\displaystyle\Phi_{t}(p(z)) =p⁡(z).\displaystyle=p(z).
(2.20) Φt​(λ​(ξ)​p​(z))\displaystyle\Phi_{t}(\lambda(\xi)p(z)) =λ⁡(ξ)∗−tp⁡(z).\displaystyle=\lambda(\xi)\ast_{-t}p(z).
